t: The seven islands passed from Koli fishing settlements to the Mauryas and later Indian dynasties, to the Delhi and Gujarat sultanates, to the Portuguese in 1535 and to the English Crown in 1661, which leased them to the East India Company in 1668.

The Company made Bombay a port and its main base on the west coast, and the Hornby Vellard of 1784, the railway of 1853 and the cotton boom of the 1860s turned the islands into one large trading city.

Bombay hosted the first session of the Indian National Congress in 1885, became the capital of Maharashtra in 1960 and took the name Mumbai in the 1990s, after riots and bombings that killed many of its people.
dyk: The seven islands of Bombay were joined into a single landmass by the Hornby Vellard, an engineering project begun in 1782 that was first rejected by the East India Company in 1783 and was completed in 1784.
ev: The islands become part of the Maurya Empire under Ashoka
The Silhara dynasty of Konkan begins to rule the region, holding it until 1260
The islands are ceded to the Portuguese under the Treaty of Bassein
Bombay passes to the English Crown as part of Catherine of Braganza’s dowry
The Crown leases the islands to the East India Company for £10 a year
The Hornby Vellard is completed and joins the seven islands
India’s first passenger railway opens between Bombay and Thane
Bombay becomes the capital of the new state of Maharashtra

f.founded: People lived on the islands from the Stone Age, and the islands became part of the Maurya Empire under Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE; the Koli fishing community had long inhabited them.
f.where: On the Konkan coast of western India, on what was originally an archipelago of seven islands with a deep natural harbour on the Arabian Sea, in the state of Maharashtra.
f.known: A harbour of the Konkan coast; the Kanheri Caves and Elephanta Caves; Portuguese and then British Bombay; the Hornby Vellard; India's first passenger railway; cotton mills and trade; the Indian National Congress and the independence movement; Bollywood
f.today: Mumbai is the capital of the Indian state of Maharashtra and a city of more than 12 million people.
